name: speed-dial

frames.best_why: All three labelled actions are fully expanded above the turned plus button.

tagline: Plus button spins to a cross as labelled actions fan upward.
summary: A round floating button that opens a vertical stack of quick actions. The plus rotates into a close cross while Share, Copy and Like slide up with their labels, arriving one after another.
appearance: A round white button with a black plus sits low on a dark stage. Opened, three circular outlined icon buttons stack above it, each with a small rounded label sitting to its left.
behaviour: Clicking the plus rotates it into a cross and reveals the stack, whose items fade and slide in with a short stagger. Picking an action collapses the stack, spins the trigger back and prints a status line above it.
demo_content: Status line "Open the menu to see quick actions" over Share, Copy and Like actions.
search_phrases: floating action button with quick actions
plus button that fans out options
quick action menu that fans out
expandable stack of buttons on click
quick action menu from one circle
use_when: One obvious action should stay in reach while a few secondary actions hide until the user asks for them.
avoid_when: It needs clear space above the trigger, and with many actions the stack can run off the top of a short panel.
customise: Side, click-or-hover opening, delay, offset, gap and disabled go on the root; each item's icon, label and on-select handler are children. The rotate angle and stagger timing need edits.
weight_why: A few buttons driven by CSS transitions; nothing runs while the dial is closed.

a11y.note: Menu roles, action labels and Escape-to-close are wired, but opening does not move focus into the revealed actions.

issues: Mid-animation the sliding labels overlap the demo's status text, as seen in frames 2 and 5.
The outlined action buttons sit on black with little surface contrast, so the icons read faintly.
polish_why: Crisp staggered reveal and a clean rotate, marred slightly by labels colliding with nearby text.
